update_robot_cookies.description: Add or replace cookies the robot sends when it opens pages, such as a fresh session cookie so it stays signed in to a site. Cookies with the same name are replaced; the step's output lists the cookies without their values.
update_robot_cookies.display_str_template: Update the cookies of the Browse AI robot '{0}'.
update_robot_cookies.name: update_robot_cookies

parameters.description: The ID of the robot to use (the UUID in the address bar when you open the robot on the Browse AI dashboard, or an 'id' returned by 'List robots').
parameters.name: robot_id

parameters.description: The cookies to set, each with a 'name', a 'value' and the 'domain' it is for, and optionally 'path' (/ if left out), 'expirationDate' (seconds since 1970), and 'secure', 'httpOnly' and 'hostOnly' (off if left out). A cookie export from a browser extension can be pasted as is; settings Browse AI doesn't store are dropped.
parameters.name: cookies

domain.description: The domain it is sent to, such as .example.com.

expirationDate.description: When it expires, in seconds since 1970. Leave out and Browse AI keeps it for a year.

hostOnly.description: Send it to the exact domain only, not its subdomains.

path.description: The path it is sent on. Leave out for the whole site.

cookies.description: The cookies as Browse AI stored them, without their values.

domain.description: The domain it is sent to.

expiration_date.description: When it expires, in seconds since 1970.

host_only.description: Whether it is sent to the exact domain only.

path.description: The path it is sent on.

robot_id.description: ID of the robot the cookies were set on.

description: Point a Browse AI robot at a webpage and get structured data back, no scraper to write. Run a robot on demand or over a whole list of pages at once, read the text fields, tables, and screenshots it captured, schedule monitors that watch pages for changes, and have Browse AI call a webhook when a task finishes.
